'''Ōke Okami Shrine''' (Takeokami Jinja / Ōkeokami Jinja / Ōōkami Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|Habikino|Q694308|qid=Q694308}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|Q122723|qid=Q122723}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}, and its former {{ill|Shakaku|Q10444029|qid=Q10444029}} was {{ill|Son-sha|ja|村社|qid=Q134917284}}.

It is also written as “Take Okami Shrine” (太祁於賀美神社), and enshrines {{ill|Kuraokami|Q644201|qid=Q644201|lt=Takaokami no Kami}} (a water deity).

=== History ===
This shrine appears in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}} as “Ōke Okami Shrine, Ishikawa District, {{ill|Kawachi Province|Q1047150|qid=Q1047150}}{{ill|Ishikawa district|Q11586399|qid=Q11586399|lt=Ishikawa District}},” but it is not found in the {{ill|Rikkokushi|Q1151168|qid=Q1151168|lt=Six National Histories}}, and its history before the Edo period is unknown. Both the former and current shrine sites were within old {{ill|Furuichi district|Q11411239|qid=Q11411239}}, but that reflects district-boundary changes after the Engishiki period.

Originally the shrine stood on a hill summit east of the current site, and until the Edo period it was called {{ill|Sannō Gongen|Q11470054|qid=Q11470054}} (even now, parishioners call it “Sannō Gongen”). The 1801 ({{ill|Kyōwa|Q960763|qid=Q960763}} 1) work ''{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kawachi Meisho Zue}}'' says: “Listed under Ishikawa District in the Engishiki. Now called Sannō and revered as the tutelary deity of this place.” In the early Meiji period it became a village shrine, but on November 18, 1907 (Meiji 40), it was merged ({{ill|Shrine Consolidation Policy|Q11590700|qid=Q11590700|lt=gōshi}}) into nearby village-shrine Hachiman Shrine (now {{ill|Tsuboi Hachimangū|Q11429677|qid=Q11429677}}).

At the request of former parishioners, it was rebuilt on December 1, 1955 ({{ill|1955|Q18577|qid=Q18577}}), borrowing land owned by {{ill|Daikoku-ji Temple|Q17228997|qid=Q17228997|lt=Daikoku-ji Temple}}.

After the merger, the former shrine site was sold and used for soil extraction, and the hill has nearly disappeared.
